stor.recommended_version: Minecraft Java Edition 1.19.2, the latest stable release listed as affected in the report; do not use snapshot 22w42a or a later version for this reproduction
stor.environment: Vanilla Minecraft Java Edition client running locally with a mouse or equivalent pointer input and audible game audio. Perform the reproduction entirely in the title-screen and Options interfaces; no world or server is required.
preconditions: Install and select exactly Minecraft Java Edition 1.19.2 in the Minecraft Launcher.
Use an unmodified client where possible; disable client mods and custom resource packs that replace menus or interface sounds so they do not confound the test.
Connect an audio output device, unmute the operating-system audio mixer, and set the Minecraft application output to a clearly audible but comfortable level.
Have a method ready to capture or monitor game audio during the final input sequence.
Use a mouse or input device that permits the primary button to remain continuously held while the pointer is moved.

steps.action: Start the Minecraft Launcher, select the installation for Java Edition 1.19.2, and launch the game.
steps.success_cue: Minecraft Java Edition 1.19.2 is running and has reached the main title screen.

steps.action: Open the Options screen normally so the in-game volume can be checked before recording the reproduction. Move the pointer to the center of the "Options..." button, press the left mouse button, and release it without dragging the pointer.
steps.exact_input: Left-click "Options..." normally: press and release without moving the mouse while held.
steps.success_cue: The Options screen is visible, including the FOV slider and the "Music & Sounds..." button.

steps.action: Open the sound settings by moving the pointer to "Music & Sounds..." and performing a normal click. Do not begin the test recording yet, because this is only audio preparation.
steps.exact_input: Left-click "Music & Sounds..." normally: press and release without dragging.
steps.success_cue: The Music & Sound Options screen is visible, with the "Master Volume" slider available.

steps.action: If Master Volume is muted or too low, move its slider to at least 50%. Click a point at or to the right of the slider's midpoint and release the button at that same point.
steps.exact_input: Left-click the midpoint or right half of the "Master Volume" slider.
steps.success_cue: The displayed Master Volume value is 50% or higher, and game interface audio is not muted.

steps.action: Return from Music & Sound Options by normally clicking the "Done" button at the bottom of the screen.
steps.success_cue: The general Options screen is visible again.

steps.action: Return to the main title screen by normally clicking the "Done" button at the bottom of the Options screen.
steps.success_cue: The main title screen is visible and the "Options..." button is available.

steps.action: Start game-audio capture, or otherwise begin actively monitoring the game audio. Keep capture running without interruption through the remaining steps.
steps.success_cue: Audio monitoring or recording is active while the main title screen remains visible.

steps.action: Move the mouse pointer onto the center of the main title screen's "Options..." button without pressing any mouse button.
steps.exact_input: Mouse movement only; do not click yet.
steps.success_cue: The pointer is over the "Options..." button and the button is visibly highlighted.

steps.action: Press and continuously hold the left mouse button while the pointer is on "Options...". Do not release the button when the Options screen opens.
steps.exact_input: Press and hold the left mouse button; keep it held through steps 10 and 11.
steps.success_cue: The general Options screen has opened, surrounding menu elements have rendered, and the left mouse button is still physically held down.

steps.action: While still holding the left mouse button, move the pointer upward onto the FOV slider. Identify this as the horizontal slider near the upper-left portion of the Options screen whose text begins with "FOV:"; use its label rather than relying on exact pixel coordinates.
steps.exact_input: Drag the mouse pointer onto the slider labeled "FOV:" without releasing the left mouse button.
steps.success_cue: The pointer is inside the rectangular bounds of the FOV slider, the Options screen is fully visible, and the left mouse button remains held.

steps.action: Pause pointer movement while keeping the left mouse button held, ensuring the pointer remains over the FOV slider and audio capture remains active.
steps.exact_input: Continue holding the left mouse button; do not move the pointer off the FOV slider.
steps.success_cue: The pointer is stationary over the FOV slider, the button is still held, and the recording includes the complete title-screen-to-Options transition.

steps.action: Release the left mouse button while the pointer remains over the FOV slider. Do not click again or move to another menu immediately afterward.
steps.exact_input: Release the held left mouse button over the "FOV:" slider.
steps.success_cue: The mouse button has been released over the FOV slider, the Options screen remains visible, and the audio capture contains the complete press-drag-release sequence.

stor.handoff_condition: The left mouse button has just been released over the FOV slider after being pressed on the title-screen "Options..." button and held continuously during the menu transition and pointer movement. The Options screen is still visible and audio capture is active or has preserved the entire sequence; hand control to the observation subsystem now.
uncertainties: The report does not prescribe a specific operating system, window resolution, GUI scale, or fixed pixel coordinates. The FOV slider should therefore be located by its visible "FOV:" label.
The report does not specify an audio volume value. Setting Master Volume to at least 50% is a practical choice solely to make the interface sounds readily observable.
The report lists many affected versions. This plan selects Java Edition 1.19.2 because it is the latest stable release explicitly listed as affected, while 22w42a is listed as the fix version.
Custom controls may replace the physical left mouse button, but the required action is the bound primary attack/select mouse action held continuously across the screen transition.

source_meta._title: Repeaters and comparators use wood sounds for placing/breaking despite being made mostly of stone

stor.recommended_version: Minecraft Java Edition 1.20 Pre-release 6 (the latest version explicitly listed as affected in the supplied report)
stor.environment: Vanilla Minecraft Java Edition 1.20 Pre-release 6 in a single-player Creative-mode world, using normal game audio and no resource pack that replaces block sounds. A new Superflat world is recommended only to provide a simple, unobstructed testing area; no particular seed, difficulty, dimension, or multiplayer server is required by the report.
preconditions: Install and launch the exact Java Edition version Minecraft 1.20 Pre-release 6 rather than the later fix version 23w33a.
Connect working speakers or headphones and verify that the operating system has not muted Minecraft.
Use the default Minecraft resource pack, or disable any resource pack that changes block sounds, so custom audio does not interfere with the reproduction.
Create or open a world in Creative mode. Creative mode is an execution convenience for obtaining the required blocks and is not stated as a bug requirement.
Stand in an open area where blocks can be placed and individually targeted without nearby entities, pistons, flowing fluids, or other sources of distracting sound.

Default inputs are assumed: E opens the inventory, number keys select hotbar slots, right-click uses or places a block, and left-click breaks a targeted block in Creative mode. If controls are rebound, use the corresponding configured actions.

steps.action: Confirm that the game is running the selected affected version by reading the version text displayed on the title screen before entering the test world.
steps.success_cue: The title screen identifies the running version as Minecraft 1.20 Pre-release 6.

steps.action: Create a new single-player world in Creative mode, preferably using the Superflat world type for an unobstructed test surface, and enter the world.
steps.exact_input: Singleplayer -> Create New World -> Game Mode: Creative -> World Type: Superflat (recommended) -> Create New World
steps.success_cue: The player has spawned in a Creative-mode world and surrounding terrain has rendered.

steps.action: Wait until world loading is complete before generating any test sounds. Move the player briefly and turn the camera to confirm that the game responds normally.
steps.success_cue: Nearby terrain is visible, movement responds without loading pauses, and the player is standing in an open placement area.

steps.action: Open the sound settings and make sure both the master volume and block-sound volume are above zero. Raise them to a clearly audible level if necessary, then return to the world.
steps.exact_input: Esc -> Options -> Music & Sounds -> set Master Volume and Blocks above 0% -> Done -> Done -> Back to Game
steps.success_cue: The world is visible again and Minecraft block sounds are not muted.

steps.action: Open the Creative inventory and obtain one Redstone Repeater, one Redstone Comparator, Stone, and Oak Planks. Put all four items into separate hotbar slots. The hotbar is the row of nine item slots at the bottom of the screen.
steps.exact_input: Press E; use the Creative inventory search field to search for "repeater", "comparator", "stone", and "oak planks"; place each result into a different hotbar slot; press E to close the inventory
steps.success_cue: The hotbar contains a redstone repeater, a redstone comparator, stone, and oak planks in separate slots.

steps.action: Establish an audible wood reference. Select Oak Planks, aim at the ground several blocks away from the intended target position, right-click once to place one plank, and listen to the placement sound.
steps.exact_input: Select Oak Planks with its hotbar number key or mouse wheel, then right-click the ground once
steps.success_cue: One oak-plank block is present and its placement sound event has been generated.

steps.action: Keep the crosshair aimed at the placed oak-plank block and left-click once in Creative mode to break it, listening to the breaking sound as the wood reference.
steps.success_cue: The oak-plank block has disappeared and its breaking sound event has been generated.

steps.action: Establish an audible stone reference. Select Stone, aim at the ground near the former plank position, and right-click once to place one stone block while listening to the placement sound. Leave this stone block in place because its top face will support the repeater and comparator.
steps.exact_input: Select Stone with its hotbar number key or mouse wheel, then right-click the ground once
steps.success_cue: One stone block is present, its placement sound event has been generated, and its top face is unobstructed.

steps.action: Place and break a second stone block nearby to hear an uninterrupted stone breaking reference without destroying the support block reserved for the target components.
steps.exact_input: Right-click the ground near the support block to place another Stone block, then left-click that second Stone block once
steps.success_cue: The second stone block has been removed, its breaking sound event has been generated, and the first stone support block remains in place.

steps.action: Select the Redstone Repeater in the hotbar. Aim the crosshair at the unobstructed top face of the remaining stone support block. Begin audio observation, then right-click once to place the repeater and capture its placement sound.
steps.exact_input: Select the Redstone Repeater with its hotbar number key or mouse wheel, then right-click the top face of the stone support block once
steps.success_cue: A redstone repeater is visibly resting on top of the stone support block, and one repeater placement sound event has just been generated.

steps.action: Aim directly at the thin repeater on top of the support block, not at the stone beneath it. Left-click once in Creative mode to break only the repeater while capturing its breaking sound.
steps.success_cue: The repeater has disappeared, the stone support block remains, and one repeater breaking sound event has just been generated.

steps.action: Select the Redstone Comparator in the hotbar. Aim at the now-unobstructed top face of the same stone support block and right-click once to place the comparator while capturing its placement sound.
steps.exact_input: Select the Redstone Comparator with its hotbar number key or mouse wheel, then right-click the top face of the stone support block once
steps.success_cue: A redstone comparator is visibly resting on top of the stone support block, and one comparator placement sound event has just been generated.

steps.action: Aim directly at the thin comparator on top of the support block, not at the stone beneath it. Left-click once in Creative mode to break only the comparator while capturing its breaking sound.
steps.success_cue: The comparator has disappeared, the stone support block remains, and one comparator breaking sound event has just been generated.

stor.handoff_condition: Beginning with step 10, audio observation is active. After step 13, one repeater and one comparator have each been placed and broken once, producing the four target sound events. The wood and stone reference sounds were generated beforehand, and the captured target audio is ready for the separate observation subsystem to evaluate.
uncertainties: The report does not specify a required game mode, world type, seed, dimension, coordinates, or server configuration. Single-player Creative mode and a Superflat world are practical choices that remove crafting and exploration but are not asserted requirements.

The report does not explicitly require reference blocks. Oak planks and stone are included as practical audio controls so an executor with little Minecraft knowledge can compare the target interactions with recognizable wood and stone placement/breaking sounds.

The report lists many affected versions. Minecraft 1.20 Pre-release 6 is recommended because it is the latest version explicitly included in the supplied affected-version list; the reproduction may also be executed in another exact affected version if required.
The report does not specify whether the repeater or comparator must be tested first. Repeater-first order is chosen only to make the procedure deterministic.
The Music & Sounds menu wording or arrangement may vary slightly among affected historical versions, but the only necessary audio condition is that master and block sounds are audible.

source_meta.issue links: Duplicate:inward:MC-271257:Empty bundle plays sound "Item unpacked" when right-clicked over an empty slot
source_meta._title: The "minecraft:item.bundle.remove_one" sound plays even when no items are unpacked from bundles

stor.recommended_version: Minecraft Java Edition 1.21 (an affected release listed in the report)
stor.environment: Single-player Minecraft Java Edition world. Use Survival mode with cheats enabled so the normal player inventory is shown and the supplied /give command can be executed. An integrated-server LAN session or dedicated server is not required. Audio output must be available.
preconditions: Launch exactly Minecraft Java Edition 1.21; do not perform the reproduction in 24w33a or a later version identified by the report as containing the fix.
Create a new single-player Survival world with Allow Cheats set to ON, or load an existing single-player world in which the player has permission to use /give.
Ensure at least one main-inventory or hotbar slot is empty. A newly created world with an otherwise empty inventory is suitable.
Ensure the game is not paused and the player can open chat and the inventory normally.
Ensure a working audio output device is selected and Minecraft is not muted. Under Esc -> Options -> Music & Sounds, set Master Volume and Players to audible, nonzero values.
Do not place any items into the bundle obtained during the procedure; the test requires the bundle to remain empty.

steps.action: Start Minecraft Java Edition 1.21 and enter the prepared single-player world. Wait for world loading to finish before continuing.
steps.success_cue: Terrain is rendered, the HUD is visible, and player movement and controls respond normally.

steps.action: Confirm that the inventory has at least one completely empty slot. Press the inventory action key, which is E by default, and visually locate an empty square in the main inventory grid or hotbar section. If no slot is empty, move or discard an item to create one.
steps.success_cue: The player inventory is open and at least one inventory slot contains no item icon or stack count.

steps.action: Close the inventory using the inventory action key so the supplied command can be entered through chat.
steps.success_cue: The inventory screen is closed and the normal world view is visible.

steps.action: Open in-game chat using the default chat key.
steps.success_cue: The chat input field is open and ready to accept a command.

steps.action: Enter the report's command exactly as written, including the leading slash, and press Enter once.
steps.success_cue: The command is accepted and one bundle is added to the player's inventory or hotbar. No command-permission or unknown-item error is displayed.

steps.action: Open the player inventory using the inventory action key, which is E by default.
steps.success_cue: The inventory screen is open, the newly given bundle is visible in one slot, and at least one other slot is empty.

steps.action: Verify that the bundle has not been loaded with any items. Do not right-click or place another item onto the bundle during setup.
steps.success_cue: The bundle obtained directly from the /give command remains the only required test item and no item has been inserted into it.

steps.action: Move the mouse pointer over the bundle's inventory slot and left-click once to pick up the entire bundle stack onto the mouse cursor. Do not merely select its hotbar slot.
steps.success_cue: The bundle icon follows the mouse cursor and its former inventory slot is empty.

steps.action: While continuing to hold the empty bundle on the mouse cursor, move the pointer over a different, completely empty inventory or hotbar slot. Do not click yet.
steps.success_cue: The bundle is still attached to the cursor, and the cursor is positioned over a slot that contains no item.

steps.action: With game audio audible, right-click the empty slot exactly once while the empty bundle is held on the mouse cursor. Do not repeat the click; immediately hand control to the observation subsystem after this input.
steps.exact_input: right-click once on the empty inventory slot
steps.success_cue: A single secondary-click input has been performed on an empty slot while the empty bundle was held by the cursor; no further inventory action has been taken.

stor.handoff_condition: The player inventory is still open, and the player has just right-clicked once on a completely empty inventory slot while holding an empty bundle on the mouse cursor. Begin audio observation immediately, before any additional click, inventory closure, or item movement.
uncertainties: The report lists many affected versions but does not require a particular one. Java Edition 1.21 is selected because it is an explicitly listed affected stable release; version 24w33a must not be used because the report identifies it as the fix version.

The report does not specify a game mode or world configuration. Survival mode with cheats enabled is a practical choice because it provides the standard player inventory while allowing the supplied /give command.

The exact volume slider category responsible for the item sound is not stated in the report. Keeping both Master Volume and Players at audible values avoids muting the trigger sound without changing the reproduction action.

source_meta._title: Equipping a player head, skull or carved pumpkin displays the generic "Gear equips" subtitle

stor.recommended_version: Minecraft Java Edition 1.19 Pre-release 1 (launcher version ID: 1.19-pre1)
stor.environment: Minecraft Java Edition client in a clean single-player Creative-mode world, with English (US) selected, game audio active, and subtitles enabled.
preconditions: The Minecraft Launcher can install and run historical snapshots and pre-releases.
Use exactly Java Edition 1.19 Pre-release 1; do not create or open the reproduction world in a different version.
A new single-player Creative-mode world is sufficient. The report specifies no seed, coordinates, dimension, difficulty, server, or multiplayer requirement.
The plan uses an Iron Chestplate as the report's armor comparison item and a Carved Pumpkin as the affected headwear item.
Use the configured equivalents if the default Inventory key E or other controls have been rebound.
Begin with the player's head and chest armor slots empty.

steps.action: In the Minecraft Launcher, open Installations, enable the Snapshots version category, create an installation using version 1.19-pre1, and launch that installation. Historical pre-releases are exposed through the launcher snapshot option. ([feedback.minecraft.net](https://feedback.minecraft.net/hc/en-us/articles/6319694424845-Minecraft-Java-Edition-1-19-Pre-Release-1?utm_source=openai))
steps.exact_input: Installations -> Snapshots: enabled -> New Installation -> Version: 1.19-pre1 -> Create -> Play
steps.success_cue: Minecraft reaches the main menu and identifies the running version as 1.19 Pre-release 1.

steps.action: From the main menu, create a new single-player world in Creative mode. Leave the seed and all other world-generation options at their defaults.
steps.exact_input: Singleplayer -> Create New World -> Game Mode: Creative -> Create New World
steps.success_cue: The player spawns in a newly generated world and can fly or access the Creative inventory.

steps.action: Wait before configuring or equipping anything until initial world and chunk loading has finished.
steps.success_cue: Nearby terrain is rendered, the loading overlay is gone, and movement and menu inputs respond normally.

steps.action: Open the pause menu, enter the language menu, select English (US), and confirm the selection. This keeps the subtitle language consistent with the report.
steps.success_cue: Menu labels are displayed in English and the Options screen is visible again.

steps.action: Open Music & Sounds settings and ensure Master Volume is not muted. A value such as 100% is suitable.
steps.success_cue: Master Volume displays a nonzero value.

steps.action: In Music & Sounds settings, toggle subtitles on.
steps.success_cue: The setting reads Show Subtitles: ON.

steps.action: Select Done until all option menus close and normal world view returns.
steps.success_cue: The player is back in the world with no menu open.

steps.action: Open the Creative inventory using the Inventory control.
steps.success_cue: The Creative inventory interface opens and displays category tabs and the hotbar.

steps.action: Select the Search Items tab, click its search field, and search for the comparison armor item.
steps.success_cue: An item result named Iron Chestplate is visible in the Creative inventory results.

steps.action: Hover the pointer over the Iron Chestplate result and press the hotbar key for slot 1 to copy the item into that slot.
steps.success_cue: An Iron Chestplate is visible in hotbar slot 1 at the bottom of the inventory screen.

steps.action: Select all text in the Creative inventory search field and replace it with the affected headwear item's name.
steps.success_cue: An item result named Carved Pumpkin is visible in the Creative inventory results.

steps.action: Hover the pointer over the Carved Pumpkin result and press the hotbar key for slot 2 to copy the item into that slot.
steps.success_cue: A Carved Pumpkin is visible in hotbar slot 2, while the Iron Chestplate remains in hotbar slot 1.

steps.action: Click the Survival Inventory tab in the Creative inventory. In this version, this is the chest-icon tab that opens the player inventory view containing the player model, crafting grid, and armor slots.
steps.exact_input: Left-click the chest-icon Survival Inventory tab
steps.success_cue: The player model and four vertical armor slots are visible, including the top head slot and the chest slot directly below it.

steps.action: Inspect the top head armor slot and the chest armor slot. If either contains an item, remove it to an unused inventory or hotbar slot before continuing.
steps.exact_input: If occupied: left-click the armor item, then left-click an empty inventory slot
steps.success_cue: Both the head and chest armor slots are empty; the Carved Pumpkin remains in hotbar slot 2 and the Iron Chestplate remains available in hotbar slot 1.

steps.action: Left-click the Iron Chestplate in hotbar slot 1 to attach it to the mouse cursor.
steps.success_cue: The Iron Chestplate icon follows the mouse cursor and hotbar slot 1 is empty.

steps.action: Left-click the chest armor slot beside the player model to equip the Iron Chestplate. Inventory-slot equipping is the sound-producing armor path relevant to this pre-release. ([feedback.minecraft.net](https://feedback.minecraft.net/hc/en-us/articles/6319694424845-Minecraft-Java-Edition-1-19-Pre-Release-1?utm_source=openai))
steps.success_cue: The Iron Chestplate occupies the chest armor slot, appears on the player model, and no item remains attached to the cursor.

steps.action: Immediately close the inventory so the subtitle area of the normal game view can be checked.
steps.success_cue: Normal world view returns, the player is wearing the Iron Chestplate, and a fresh subtitle notification from the comparison equip action is visible near the lower-right corner.

steps.action: Do not move, interact, or produce additional sounds. Wait until the comparison equip subtitle has completely disappeared, so it cannot be confused with the next equip event.
steps.success_cue: No subtitle from the Iron Chestplate equip action remains visible.

steps.action: Open the Creative inventory again and return to the Survival Inventory tab if the armor slots are not already displayed.
steps.exact_input: E, then left-click the chest-icon Survival Inventory tab if needed
steps.success_cue: The armor slots are visible, the Iron Chestplate remains in the chest slot, the head slot is empty, and the Carved Pumpkin is present in hotbar slot 2.

steps.action: Left-click the Carved Pumpkin in hotbar slot 2 to attach it to the mouse cursor.
steps.success_cue: The Carved Pumpkin icon follows the mouse cursor, hotbar slot 2 is empty, and the head armor slot remains empty.

steps.action: Left-click the top head armor slot to equip the Carved Pumpkin. Official notes for this exact pre-release identify placing pumpkins or skulls into the headwear slot as the relevant sound-producing action. ([feedback.minecraft.net](https://feedback.minecraft.net/hc/en-us/articles/6319694424845-Minecraft-Java-Edition-1-19-Pre-Release-1?utm_source=openai))
steps.exact_input: Left-click the top head armor slot
steps.success_cue: The Carved Pumpkin occupies the head armor slot, appears on the player model, and no item remains attached to the cursor.

steps.action: Immediately close the inventory without clicking, moving items, or performing any other sound-producing action.
steps.success_cue: Normal world view has just returned, the Carved Pumpkin is equipped, and no unrelated action has occurred since the headwear equip action.

stor.handoff_condition: The Carved Pumpkin has just been placed into the player's head armor slot in Java Edition 1.19 Pre-release 1, and the inventory has immediately been closed. Begin subtitle observation before the equip-event subtitle fades.
uncertainties: The report does not specify a game mode, world seed, dimension, difficulty, or server type; a new single-player Creative world is used only as the simplest deterministic way to obtain the required items.
The report permits any armor piece or elytra for the comparison action. This plan uses an Iron Chestplate so the head slot remains free for the affected item.

The report permits a player head, another skull, or a carved pumpkin for the affected action. This plan tests a Carved Pumpkin; the alternate head and skull variants would require separate repetitions after clearing the head slot and waiting for the previous subtitle to disappear.
Default Java Edition keyboard and mouse bindings are described; rebound controls must use their configured equivalents.

source_meta._title: Subtitles string "subtitles.block.trial_spawner.spawn_mob" is misleading and inconsistent

stor.environment: Vanilla Minecraft Java Edition 1.20.4 in a new single-player world, using English (United States), the built-in Update 1.21 experimental data pack, default resource assets, Creative mode for deterministic setup, and Survival mode for activation.
preconditions: Use an unmodified Minecraft Java Edition 1.20.4 client; disable mods and resource packs that could replace language or sound assets.
Create a disposable test world rather than using an important existing save.
Use the English (United States) language so the report's English translation for subtitles.block.trial_spawner.spawn_mob is exercised.
The reproduction requires subtitles to be enabled and the player to be in Survival mode when the configured Trial Spawner is approached.
Commands must be available because the setup changes the player from Creative mode to Survival mode.

steps.action: Launch Minecraft Java Edition 1.20.4. At the main menu, open Options, select Language, choose English (United States), and click Done until the main menu is shown again.
steps.success_cue: The main-menu text is displayed in English and the lower-left version label identifies Minecraft 1.20.4.

steps.action: Select Singleplayer, then Create New World. Set Game Mode to Creative so the required experimental block and spawn egg can be obtained without exploration. Leave commands enabled; Creative worlds normally provide command access.
steps.success_cue: The world-creation screen shows Creative as the selected game mode.

steps.action: From the world-creation screen, open Data Packs. In the available built-in packs, select the pack displayed as Update 1.21, also identifiable as update_1_21, and move it into the selected/enabled list. Click Done. Accept the experimental-feature warning if one appears. Java experimental features are enabled from the Data Packs screen. ([minecraft.net](https://www.minecraft.net/en-us/article/testing-new-minecraft-features))
steps.success_cue: The Update 1.21 pack is in the selected data-pack list and the world-creation screen can be continued.

steps.action: For a deterministic open spawning area, open the world settings and set World Type to Superflat. Leave Difficulty at Normal or another non-Peaceful setting.
steps.success_cue: The world-creation screen shows Superflat and a non-Peaceful difficulty.

steps.action: Click Create New World. If another experimental-settings confirmation appears, choose the option that proceeds with world creation. Wait until the world has loaded, surrounding terrain is rendered, and movement responds normally.
steps.success_cue: The player is standing in a loaded, flat Overworld in Creative mode and can move normally.

steps.action: Press Esc, select Options, then Accessibility Settings. Set Show Subtitles to ON. Click Done until gameplay resumes.
steps.success_cue: The Accessibility Settings screen showed Show Subtitles: ON before returning to gameplay.

steps.action: Press E to open the Creative inventory. Open the Search Items tab, click its search field, enter "trial spawner", left-click the Trial Spawner result, and left-click hotbar slot 1 to place the block there. The hotbar is the row of nine item slots along the bottom of the gameplay screen.
steps.success_cue: A Trial Spawner item is present in hotbar slot 1.

steps.action: While the Creative inventory remains open, replace the search text with "zombie spawn egg". Left-click the Zombie Spawn Egg result and place it in hotbar slot 2, then press E to close the inventory.
steps.success_cue: The inventory is closed, with a Trial Spawner in hotbar slot 1 and a Zombie Spawn Egg in hotbar slot 2.

steps.action: Move to an unobstructed part of the flat world with several blocks of solid floor available on every side. Avoid placing the test next to walls, holes, liquids, or other entities so the Trial Spawner has clear spawn positions.
steps.success_cue: A level, open test area surrounds the player and nearby terrain is fully rendered.

steps.action: Press 1 to select the Trial Spawner. Aim the crosshair at the top of a ground block in the open area and right-click once to place the Trial Spawner.
steps.success_cue: A Trial Spawner block is visibly placed one block above the flat ground.

steps.action: Press 2 to select the Zombie Spawn Egg. Aim directly at the placed Trial Spawner and right-click it once. A Trial Spawner placed by a Creative player initially has no mob type; interacting with it while holding a spawn egg configures that mob type. ([minecraft.net](https://www.minecraft.net/en-us/article/minecraft-java-edition-1-20-3))
steps.exact_input: Default input: 2, then right-click the Trial Spawner once
steps.success_cue: The Trial Spawner displays a miniature zombie or other internal visual indicating that it is configured to spawn zombies.

steps.action: Move approximately four blocks away from the configured Trial Spawner. Face it directly and ensure no blocks obstruct the line of sight between the player and the spawner. Keep the lower-right portion of the screen unobstructed by menus.
steps.success_cue: The configured Trial Spawner is fully visible a short distance away, with open floor around it and no menu open.

steps.action: Press T to open in-game chat. Enter the exact command "/gamemode survival", including the leading slash, and press Enter. Do not move away from the Trial Spawner after executing the command.
steps.success_cue: The Survival health and hunger HUD is visible, chat has closed, and the player remains near and in direct view of the configured Trial Spawner.

steps.action: Without opening another menu or moving out of range, keep the Trial Spawner and the lower-right subtitle area visible. Wait until the Trial Spawner activates and a zombie visibly begins to appear near it. Stop all further input at the instant the first mob is spawned; that spawn is the sound/subtitle trigger to be inspected.
steps.success_cue: A zombie has just been produced by the Trial Spawner while the player remains nearby in Survival mode with subtitles enabled.

stor.handoff_condition: The configured Trial Spawner has just spawned its first zombie while the player is nearby in Survival mode, Show Subtitles remains ON, and the lower-right subtitle area is visible. Hand control to the observation subsystem immediately at the spawn event without performing further input.
uncertainties: The report supplies no world seed, coordinates, generated Trial Chamber, or mob type. This plan therefore uses a manually placed Trial Spawner configured with a Zombie Spawn Egg in a superflat world as the minimum deterministic implementation.

The report does not explicitly mention enabling the Update 1.21 experimental data pack, but the Trial Spawner is an experimental feature in the recommended affected version, so the pack is enabled as a verified execution requirement.

The Mojira comment provides /tellraw @s {"translate":"subtitles.block.trial_spawner.spawn_mob"} as an alternate way to render the translation. That alternate is not used here because the primary reproduction specifically exercises the subtitle generated by a real Trial Spawner mob-spawn event.
